# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(11)

# Number of observations to simulate
n <- 500

CREATE VARIABLES

# Simulate independent variables with realistic ranges
temperature     <- runif(n, min = 25, max = 40)         # °C
pH                <- runif(n, min = 4.0, max = 6.5)     # pH
glucose_concentration <- runif(n, min = 50, max = 150)  # g/L
fermentation_time <- runif(n, min = 12, max = 72)       # hours

# Pre-allocate ethanol_yield vector
ethanol_yield <- numeric(n)

Define Parameters Based on Biological Knowledge of S. cerevisiae

for (i in 1:n) {
  # Maximum theoretical ethanol yield: ~0.51 g ethanol / g glucose
  # Real fermentation achieves ~85% due to growth & maintenance
  theoretical_max_yield_per_g_glucose <- 0.51
  efficiency <- 0.85
  
  # Optimal temperature: ~32.5°C
  temp_opt <- 32.5
  temp_response <- dnorm(temperature[i], mean = temp_opt, sd = 3)
  temp_factor <- temp_response / dnorm(temp_opt, sd = 3)  # normalized
  
  # Optimal pH: ~5.0
  pH_opt <- 5.0
  pH_response <- dnorm(pH[i], mean = pH_opt, sd = 0.5)
  pH_factor <- pH_response / dnorm(pH_opt, sd = 0.5)  # normalized
  
  # Time factor: increases with time, plateaus after ~60 hours
  time_factor <- plogis(fermentation_time[i], location = 48, scale = 8)
  time_factor <- time_factor / plogis(48, location = 48, scale = 8)  # normalize to 1
  
  # Glucose inhibition: osmotic stress >120 g/L
  glucose_factor <- ifelse(
    glucose_concentration[i] > 120,
    1 - 0.3 * ((glucose_concentration[i] - 120) / 30),
    1
  )
  glucose_factor <- pmax(glucose_factor, 0.6)  # floor at 0.6
  
  # ✅ CRITICAL: Include theoretical yield and efficiency
  base_yield <- glucose_concentration[i] * 
    theoretical_max_yield_per_g_glucose * 
    efficiency * 
    temp_factor * 
    pH_factor * 
    time_factor * 
    glucose_factor
  
  # Add realistic noise (3% of yield)
  noise <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 0.03 * base_yield)
  ethanol_yield[i] <- pmax(base_yield + noise, 0)  # non-negative
}

# Combine into a data frame
fermentation_data <- tibble(
  temperature = round(temperature, 1),
  pH = round(pH, 2),
  glucose_concentration = round(glucose_concentration, 1),
  fermentation_time = round(fermentation_time, 1),
  ethanol_yield = round(ethanol_yield, 2)
)

Part 2: Data Visualization in R

# Set theme
theme_set(theme_minimal())

# Create grouping variables
fermentation_data <- fermentation_data %>%
  mutate(
    time_group = cut(fermentation_time,
                     breaks = c(12, 24, 48, 72),
                     labels = c("Short (12–24h)", "Medium (24–48h)", "Long (48–72h)"),
                     include.lowest = TRUE),
    pH_group = cut(pH,
                   breaks = c(4.0, 4.8, 5.6, 6.5),
                   labels = c("Low pH (4.0–4.8)", "Medium pH (4.8–5.6)", "High pH (5.6–6.5)"),
                   include.lowest = TRUE),
    glucose_level = cut(glucose_concentration,
                        breaks = c(50, 80, 110, 150),
                        labels = c("Low (50–80)", "Medium (80–110)", "High (110–150)"),
                        include.lowest = TRUE)
  )

Ethanol Yield vs. Temperature

p1 <- ggplot(fermentation_data, aes(x = temperature, y = ethanol_yield)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = ethanol_yield), alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "Yield") +
  geom_smooth(method = 'loess', se = TRUE, color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Ethanol Yield vs. Temperature",
    x = "Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Ethanol Yield (g/L)",
    caption = "Peak yield near 32–35°C"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(25, 40, by = 2))

p1

Heatmap: Ethanol Yield by Temperature and pH (Faceted by Glucose)

# Bin for smoother heatmap
yield_summary <- fermentation_data %>%
  mutate(
    temperature_bin = round(temperature / 0.5) * 0.5,
    pH_bin = round(pH / 0.2) * 0.2
  ) %>%
  group_by(temperature_bin, pH_bin, glucose_level) %>%
  summarise(mean_yield = mean(ethanol_yield), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(temperature_bin, pH_bin, glucose_level) %>%
  rename(temperature = temperature_bin, pH = pH_bin)

p5 <- ggplot(yield_summary, aes(x = temperature, y = pH, fill = mean_yield)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "Avg Yield (g/L)") +
  facet_wrap(~ glucose_level) +
  labs(title = "Ethanol Yield by Temperature and pH", x = "Temp (°C)", y = "pH") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

p5

Part 3: Statistical Modeling

# Add centered quadratic terms
fermentation_data <- fermentation_data %>%
  mutate(
    temp_centered = temperature - mean(temperature),
    temp2 = temp_centered^2,
    pH_centered = pH - mean(pH),
    pH2 = pH_centered^2
  )

# Fit model with quadratic terms
model_centered <- lm(
  ethanol_yield ~ temp_centered + temp2 + pH_centered + pH2 +
    glucose_concentration + fermentation_time,
  data = fermentation_data
)

# Model summary
summary(model_centered)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = ethanol_yield ~ temp_centered + temp2 + pH_centered + 
##     pH2 + glucose_concentration + fermentation_time, data = fermentation_data)
## 
## Residuals:
##        Min         1Q     Median         3Q        Max

## temp2                 -4.306e+46  3.918e+45 -10.989  < 2e-16 ***
## pH_centered           -5.591e+47  8.258e+46  -6.771 3.66e-11 ***

## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

vif(model_centered)

beta_coeffs

Part 5: Machine Learning with Random Forest

# Prepare data
predictors <- c("temp_centered", "temp2", "pH_centered", "pH2",
                "glucose_concentration", "fermentation_time")
ml_data <- dplyr::select(fermentation_data, all_of(predictors), ethanol_yield)

# Train Random Forest
set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  ethanol_yield ~ .,
  data = ml_data,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

# Predictions
lm_pred <- predict(model_centered, newdata = fermentation_data)
rf_pred <- predict(rf_model, newdata = ml_data)
actual <- fermentation_data$ethanol_yield

# Metrics
get_metrics <- function(actual, pred, name) {
  data.frame(
    Model = name,
    RMSE = round(rmse(actual, pred), 3),
    MAE = round(mae(actual, pred), 3),
    R2 = round(cor(actual, pred)^2, 3)
  )
}

performance <- bind_rows(
  get_metrics(actual, lm_pred, "Linear Model"),
  get_metrics(actual, rf_pred, "Random Forest")
)
performance
##           Model         RMSE          MAE    R2
## 1  Linear Model 1.356292e+48 9.417953e+47 0.543
## 2 Random Forest 3.279282e+47 1.704371e+47 0.986
# Plot predictions
comparison <- tibble(actual, linear = lm_pred, random_forest = rf_pred) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(linear, random_forest), names_to = "Model", values_to = "Predicted")

ggplot(comparison, aes(x = actual, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model) +
  labs(title = "Actual vs Predicted Ethanol Yield") +
  theme_minimal()

# Variable importance
varImpPlot(rf_model, main = "RF: Variable Importance")

summary(model_centered)
